title: Modern music and today's trombonists
summary: Palmer's view on modern bands lacking foundation, coming back to playing, and Percy Jackson.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: What do you think about Bach and all this new junk they play nowadays?

This new stuff is alright, this new stuff is alright. On the synth, the new stuff they got now, they ain't got no, you might say, no foundation. They ain't got no foundation. Everybody's jumping up and out and in and up, you know, and you can't, you can't tell, you can't get the significance of the piece, you know. That's a hard tune. Yeah, you don't know what they're playing, you can't tell what they're playing. There ain't no lead. And the fellow that's playing the lead should be playing the lead. He's jumping from here and different places, you see. And you can't, you can't tell what they're playing. But you get one band that has a good lead, and then them fellas playing that other junk, you know, see. It's better, it's all better, you know. Yeah, we had a nice band.
Yeah, I'd like to hear you with a real good...
I'll wait some days to practice up and get together. Get together.

It wouldn't take you long, I don't believe, to get back in shape as far as the... I don't think so, no. I mean, anybody really knows something, as they say, you never forget it. No, you never forget it. Like they say, for instance, riding a bicycle, if you've never ridden for ten years, you can get on a bicycle. Try to get on a bicycle and go right on. And they say, you can't swim like me, you're like me. But they say, if you once learned to swim when you were a kid, maybe fifty years later, somebody will push you in the water and you'll swim. You go right on, eh? You learn how to do it. And I know with your music, you can pick up that trombone again. It might take you, well, a couple of weeks to get you in there, to get shape, maybe. Yeah, it'd take you in about a couple of weeks, I guess, Mike.

But still, it'd be better than almost anybody can do now. Oh, yeah. I've never heard, I'm sure. Yeah, these fellas are playing now. I don't know. I'm not knocking, I'm not knocking like that. But, I don't know, they don't seem to get the right bass on, you know, on trombone. It seem like they're off some way. It seem like they're way back. And sometimes I pick up, sometime on the radio, hear some fellas playing, and he's alright, but there's a few of them, see? Yeah. And the majority, they look like as many bands as they got, look like they ought to always have good trombone. Yeah, I'd think so. But it's hard to get a good trombone player. Now, Percy Jackson, he's a nice trombone player. Yeah. He plays nice trombone. He took lessons from you, too, here in Chicago. Yeah, he sure did. Uh-huh. Yeah, he did.
